name: Project Structure & Tooling
blurb: You can scaffold a Python project with uv, src layout and lockfiles that another engineer can clone and run first try.

name: Typed Python
blurb: You can use type hints and dataclasses as design tools, and make a messy module pass strict type checking without papering over its bugs.

name: Errors & Failure Design
blurb: You can design an exception hierarchy, chain causes with raise-from, and parse junk input without losing rows silently.

name: Validation with Pydantic
blurb: You can validate every input at the boundary with Pydantic models and load configuration from the environment without secrets in code.

name: Testing & Mocking
blurb: You can write fixture-driven, parametrized tests that pin behaviour and stub the network, so refactoring stops being scary.

name: Async & Concurrency
blurb: You can run bounded-concurrency I/O with asyncio and spot the blocking call that quietly serialises an async service.

name: HTTP Semantics & Clients
blurb: You can pick the right status code and method for a situation and drive a remote API with timeouts and safe retry policy.

name: FastAPI Services
blurb: You can build a typed FastAPI service with dependency injection, response models, a consistent error envelope and streaming endpoints.

name: Auth, Rate Limits & Idempotency
blurb: You can protect an endpoint with API keys, request ids, per-key rate limits and idempotency keys that survive a retrying client.

name: SQL & ORM with Postgres
blurb: You can model an application schema in SQLAlchemy, manage transactions, and evolve the database with reviewed Alembic migrations.

name: Caching & Cache Keys
blurb: You can cache expensive answers in Redis with a key that encodes every input the answer depends on, and invalidate it on reindex.

name: Queues & Workers
blurb: You can move heavy work out of request handlers into arq workers with job ids, status endpoints, dedupe and safe webhook intake.

name: LLM APIs & Resilient Client
blurb: You can call either major vendor behind one interface, stream responses, and wrap it in a client with retries, timeouts and fallbacks.

name: Prompt & Context Engineering
blurb: You can write versioned prompts with explicit output contracts and pack a context window by priority instead of by hope.

name: Structured Outputs
blurb: You can make a model return JSON you can trust by making a Pydantic schema the contract, with a repair path for the rest.

name: Cost & Latency Engineering
blurb: You can price a workload per thousand requests, cut it with prompt caching, and defend a model choice with a bench table.

name: Embeddings & Vector Search
blurb: You can embed text, rank it by cosine similarity, name the query types embeddings fail on, and store vectors in a real vector database.

name: Chunking & Ingestion
blurb: You can turn real PDFs into clean, structure-aware chunks whose boundaries keep facts and their labels together.

name: Retrieval, Hybrid & Reranking
blurb: You can diagnose a retrieval failure from its symptom and fix it with query rewriting, BM25 fusion and a cross-encoder rerank stage.

name: Grounding & Citations
blurb: You can answer strictly from retrieved context, cite the chunk behind every claim, and refuse honestly when the context is silent.

name: Tool Calling
blurb: You can hand-roll the tool-call loop, write tool schemas and descriptions the model actually obeys, and keep results honest.

name: Workflow Patterns & Judgment
blurb: You can build chains, routers and orchestrators, and argue from your own measurements when an agent is the wrong tool.

name: Agent Loops & State
blurb: You can write an agent loop with termination guards, persist its transcript for resume, and gate consequential actions behind approval.

name: Golden Datasets
blurb: You can build a gold set with difficulty tags, expected sources and unanswerable cases that a domain expert would sign off.

name: Retrieval Metrics
blurb: You can score retrieval with recall@k and MRR and prove whether a pipeline change actually helped on the same gold set.

name: LLM-as-Judge
blurb: You can design a rubric judge for groundedness and correctness, calibrate it against your own labels, and name its biases.

name: Regression Gates & Error Analysis
blurb: You can run evals as code with thresholds that fail loudly, then read the worst transcripts and fix the failure category.

name: Prompt Injection Defence
blurb: You can attack your own retrieval and agent paths with indirect injection, then layer mitigations and state the residual risk plainly.

name: Secrets, PII & Tenancy
blurb: You can keep secrets out of code and logs, redact PII before it is written, and enforce tenant isolation at the data layer with a test.

name: Resilience Patterns
blurb: You can apply backoff with jitter, a circuit breaker and a fallback ladder so a provider blip degrades instead of cascading.

name: Observability & Tracing
blurb: You can emit structured logs and correlated traces across API, queue and worker, and read a latency tree to find the real bottleneck.

name: Systematic Debugging
blurb: You can reproduce a failure, isolate it with a debugger or a trace, and fix the class of bug rather than the instance.

name: Docker & Compose
blurb: You can containerize an API and its worker with cache-friendly layers and bring the whole stack up with one compose command.

name: CI/CD & Deploy
blurb: You can run lint, tests and an eval smoke on every pull request and ship the merged result to a public URL automatically.

name: AI Architecture
blurb: You can take a vague AI requirement to a defended component diagram with data flows, failure modes and a written decision record.

name: Capacity & Cost Modelling
blurb: You can do the napkin math for tokens, storage, workers and spend at a given user count, and show which assumption dominates.

name: Multi-Tenant Platform Build
blurb: You can assemble ingestion, retrieval, assistant mode, jobs and per-tenant isolation into one platform that holds together under load.

name: Discovery & Scoping
blurb: You can run a discovery conversation that finds the business problem, the data reality and the disqualifiers before any solution talk.

name: Proposals, ROI & Risk
blurb: You can write a build-versus-buy case, a ranged cost model and a risk register that a sceptical client would actually sign.

name: Case Method & Interview Craft
blurb: You can work an unseen client case end to end under time pressure and turn your own projects into bullets and stories that survive follow-up.
